request.spec:
An OPEN claim can no longer be edited; only a DRAFT can, and the edit of an open claim is refused
with an error on the claim. To change an open claim, void it and add a new one. A voided claim now
keeps its number (it is still never reused), and CLAIM_VOIDED carries it.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
An OPEN claim can no longer be edited; only a DRAFT can, and the edit of an open claim is refused
with an error on the claim. To change an open claim, void it and add a new one. A voided claim now
keeps its number (it is still never reused), and CLAIM_VOIDED carries it.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Only draft claims can be edited now, and a voided claim keeps its number. All 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

**Server**
- `SaveClaim.java` refuses to edit any claim that isn't a DRAFT (`a OPEN claim cannot be edited`), so nothing is saved and nothing goes to the audit file. The database update in `ClaimRepository.update` also only matches DRAFT rows, as a second guard.
- `ChangeClaimStatus.java` no longer clears the number when a claim is voided. `CLAIM_VOIDED` now ends with `number=<n>` when the claim had one. A draft that's voided never had a number, so its line stays as before. I removed the unused `clearNumber` method from the repository.

**Front end** (`claims.slot.tsx`)
- Pressing Edit on a claim that isn't a draft shows `claim-error` on that claim's row ("only a DRAFT claim can be edited"), and the editor doesn't open. The error clears on the next action on that row or when the claim form is submitted.
- I first refused the edit only when it was saved, but then the test saw two error elements at once and failed. Refusing when Edit is pressed fixed that; the server check still covers direct requests.

The change also applies to SETTLED and VOID claims, which could be edited before. Claims voided before this change already had their number wiped in the database, and I can't restore it, so those will still show no number.
